_doc: Evidence-based pins from 114 photos analyzed. Status: confirmed = direct visual proof; candidate = was in plan but no photo proof; downgraded = previously assumed but evidence contradicts.

trip.title: Japan — April 2026
trip.subtitle: Bryan's first time in Japan · 10 days · Tokyo + Kyoto
trip.kyoto_companions: 2 women in Apr 25 selfie — likely Clair + 1 other (TBC)

facts.kid: Tokyo's fanciest district — land here costs $1 million per square meter!
facts.tip: Bryan's hotel: Mitsui Garden Hotel Ginza Tsukiji (10 nights)
facts.wow: Ginza's main street closes to traffic every Sat/Sun afternoon, becoming a 'pedestrian paradise' (hokoten) since 1970.
facts.local: Locals don't really shop here - they come for department-store basement food halls (depachika) and dinners.

facts.kid: Tokyo's most famous KABUKI theater — traditional Japanese drama with elaborate costumes & makeup, in a beautiful century-old building.
facts.tip: You walked past it at 10 PM your first night — right next to your hotel
facts.wow: Full shows can run 5-6 hours; locals buy 'one-act' tickets (~Y1,000) for just 30-60 min when they don't have all day.
facts.local: The current building is the FIFTH on the same plot - earthquakes, fires, and WW2 bombing rebuilt it in 1925, 1951, and 2013.

facts.kid: A giant red-brick station that's 100+ years old. Where Bryan's shinkansen to Kyoto and back arrived/departed.
facts.tip: Departed Apr 25 morning + Arrived Apr 26 17:15 from Kyoto on NOZOMI 28
facts.wow: The red-brick Marunouchi facade is from 1914; it was bombed in WW2 and only fully restored to original spec in 2012.
facts.local: Locals never just say 'Tokyo Station' - they specify 'Yaesu side' (east) or 'Marunouchi side' (west). The two sides feel like different cities.

facts.kid: Tokyo's Wall Street — giant office buildings + MUJI mega-store + Imperial Palace next door.
facts.tip: You walked here Apr 22 4:53 PM after the Cabinet Office (CAO) meeting
facts.wow: About 90% of land here is owned by ONE landlord: Mitsubishi Estate, since 1894 - reportedly the highest-value real estate block on Earth.
facts.local: This is salaryman lunch country. The 2nd-basement food courts in every office tower hide the best ramen and donburi shops.

facts.kid: Where the Emperor of Japan lives! Garden was the inner part of a giant samurai castle.
facts.history: Built on Edo Castle, where shoguns ruled for 250 years.
facts.tip: Apr 19 afternoon long stone-walled embankment photo could be here OR Hamarikyu
facts.wow: At the 1989 peak, the land beneath the palace was reportedly valued at more than ALL real estate in California combined.
facts.local: The 5 km inner-moat loop is Tokyo's most popular running route - any morning you'll pass dozens of runners.

facts.kid: An old Edo-era garden right on Tokyo Bay! Has a teahouse on a tiny island in a saltwater pond.
facts.tip: Best fit for the Apr 19 2:23 PM pond photo (closest to Tsukiji hotel)
facts.wow: The pond connects to Tokyo Bay so the water level rises and falls with the tides - one of only a few tidal saltwater garden ponds in Japan.
facts.local: The 300-year-old pine near the entrance (sanbyaku-nen no matsu) was personally planted by a Tokugawa shogun.

facts.kid: Used to be the BIGGEST fish market in the world. Sushi for breakfast!
facts.tip: You walked here at 5:52 AM Apr 19 BEFORE it opened — sunrise market walk
facts.wow: The famous tuna auction moved to Toyosu in 2018, but the OUTER market stayed - and it's busier than ever.
facts.local: Tsukiji shop owners arrive at 3-4 AM. If you want the best stuff, be there by 8 - by 10 the tourists have it.

facts.kid: Tokyo's OLDEST temple — built in 645 AD! Bryan visited TWICE: Apr 19 daylight & Apr 27 sunrise. The whole trip was bookended by Senso-ji.
facts.history: Founded when two fisherman brothers pulled a tiny golden statue of Kannon from the Sumida River.
facts.ritual: Wave incense smoke over yourself before entering for good health.
facts.symbol: 1,500-lb red lantern at Kaminarimon Gate ('Thunder Gate').
facts.wow: A typhoon ripped the giant Kaminarimon lantern in half in 2014. The temple replaces it every ~10 years and ceremonially burns the old one.
facts.local: Skip the main path. Cut one block west to Denpoin-dori to see what Asakusa looked like a century ago.

facts.kid: Old shopping street with snacks, fans, toys. 250+ years old, ~90 little shops.
facts.food: Try ningyo-yaki (doll-shaped cake), age-manju, senbei rice crackers.
facts.wow: Many of the 250+ shops have hereditary licenses - same families running them for 6+ generations.
facts.local: Last shop on the right before the gate (Funawa) does the best age-manju in Tokyo, fried while you wait.

facts.kid: A hidden Edo-era side street near Senso-ji that most tourists skip. You found it Apr 19 11:31 — kanji photo confirmed (伝法院通)
facts.wow: Zero chain stores - strict preservation rules keep the whole street Edo-period in appearance.
facts.local: The maneki-neko cat figurines on the rooftops aren't decoration - they're inviting business luck for each shop below.

facts.kid: Tokyo's iconic river that runs through Asakusa — the river the Senso-ji statue legend started in!
facts.tip: Walked here right after Senso-ji at 11:39 AM Apr 19
facts.wow: Until 1888, sumo wrestlers actually fought on barges floating on this river.
facts.local: From May the Suijo Bus runs Asakusa to Hamarikyu - same route Bryan walked, seen from the water.

facts.kid: An ancient Buddhist temple right next to TOKYO TOWER. The view of the temple's curved black roof with the red-and-white Tokyo Tower behind is one of Tokyo's most iconic photos.
facts.history: Founded 1393. Family temple of the Tokugawa shoguns. Six shoguns are buried here.
facts.symbol: Hundreds of small Jizo statues with red bibs and pinwheels — memorials for unborn or deceased children
facts.ritual: Pray for safe passage of children and family
facts.wow: Tokyo Tower is 13m TALLER than the Eiffel Tower (333m vs 320m) and was built in 1958 specifically to top it.
facts.local: The little Jizo statues with red bibs are memorials for unborn children. Parents change the bibs themselves, year after year.

facts.kid: Busiest crosswalk in the world! Up to 3,000 people cross at once.
facts.tip: Likely Apr 22 6:53 PM rainy walk based on neon district + S.RIDE taxi
facts.wow: Up to 3,000 people cross at once during peak - one of the most photographed urban spaces on Earth.
facts.local: Locals avoid the scramble itself; they cross on the 2nd-floor pedestrian bridges and station underpasses to skip the crowd.

facts.kid: A huge forest shrine with 100,000 trees in Tokyo!
facts.deity: Spirits of Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken
facts.wow: The 100,000-tree forest was donated from every prefecture in 1920 - it's a fake 'old forest,' only a century old.
facts.local: Saturday mornings you'll often see a full white-kimono wedding procession crossing the main path - locals plan around it.

facts.kid: Shinjuku Station is the BUSIEST train station on Earth — 3.5M people daily!
facts.wow: Shinjuku Station has 200+ exits - even Tokyoites routinely take the wrong one and end up 10+ min from where they meant to be.
facts.local: Skip the west side (skyscrapers). The east side - Kabukicho, Golden Gai, Omoide Yokocho - is where Tokyo nightlife actually happens.

facts.kid: Tokyo's electronics + anime + manga district! Tons of stores stacked vertically.
facts.tip: Apr 21 dinner at IBREN restaurant — receipt confirmed Kanda-Sakumacho 3-38
facts.wow: Until 1989 this was Tokyo's wholesale electronics PARTS district. Anime/manga took over only after 2000.
facts.local: Multi-floor stores hide collector-only material on upper floors. Ground floor = casual; 5th floor = serious. Don't skip the elevator.

facts.kid: Japan's Ministry of Defense — like the Pentagon. Bryan met with the Defense Innovation Hub team here.
facts.tip: Apr 24 1:30 PM meeting — visitor badge + martial arts poster confirmed
facts.wow: The MoD sits on the site of the old Imperial Army HQ - where Tojo (the WW2 PM) had his office.
facts.local: The Ichigaya Memorial Hall on the grounds is where Mishima Yukio committed seppuku in 1970. Open by reservation only.

facts.kid: Tokyo's government district — like Washington DC's federal buildings.
facts.tip: Apr 22 2 PM CAO meeting
facts.wow: Every Japanese ministry HQ sits on this 0.8 sq km - the most concentrated bureaucratic real estate on Earth.
facts.local: Kasumigaseki salarymen work the latest hours in Japan. 11 PM and 80% of office lights are still on.

facts.kid: Your first dinner in Japan — a tablet-order Tokyo izakaya. You had Iyoshi Cola (Japan's craft cola).
facts.tip: Apr 18 9:50 PM. Sober: cola + water.
facts.wow: Iyoshi Cola was invented in 2018 by a fourth-generation Chinese-herb pharmacist - it's a literal craft cola from Tokyo.
facts.local: Tablet-order izakaya only became normal post-2020. Older locals still find them rude.

facts.kid: A pub-style restaurant in Akihabara where Bryan had jasmine tea while co-workers had drinks.
facts.tip: Receipt confirmed Apr 21 9:32 PM. Total ¥8,514 (cash). Phone 03-58254520. Table C1.
facts.wow: 'Izakaya' literally means 'stay-sake-shop' - originally sake shops that let you drink on-site instead of buying to go.
facts.local: The 'free' otoshi appetizer that appears is NOT free - it's the table charge in food form, Y300-500/person.

facts.kid: A traditional Japanese grilled-chicken-skewer place. Bryan saw exotic cuts on the menu — quail eggs, knee cartilage, the bit between heart and liver!
facts.tip: Apr 22 8:07 PM. After the rainy Tokyo nightlife wander.
facts.wow: Real yakitori specialists use 30+ DIFFERENT chicken parts - organs Western butchers throw away.
facts.local: Order 'omakase' (chef's choice) for the full course. Picking individual skewers off the menu marks you as a tourist.

facts.kid: A traditional multi-course Japanese dinner — sashimi, grilled fish, tiny artistic dishes — with the NSSOL business team.
facts.tip: Apr 23 7:35-8:24 PM. Group photo at the zen-style restaurant with the NSSOL team.
facts.wow: Kaiseki has 9-13 strict courses in fixed order (appetizer to sashimi to grilled to simmered to fried to vinegared to rice to soup to dessert) - same sequence since the 1500s.
facts.local: Pink-purple nails on a Japanese businesswoman are often a fintech, design, or international-firm signal - corporate Japan still leans conservative.

facts.kid: Where you had your 'best dinner ever' (your handwritten words!). Wagyu shabu-shabu — thinly sliced beef cooked in dashi broth at the table.
facts.tip: Apr 24 7:38-10:23 PM. Signed menu from the table. WAGYU BURGER doodle.
facts.wow: 'Shabu-shabu' is onomatopoeia - the SOUND of beef swishing in broth.
facts.local: Wagyu shabu at this tier runs Y15-30K/person. A signed menu makes it a milestone meal in Tokyo.

facts.kid: A wagyu beef restaurant from a 5-generation family — the meat-merchant tradition started in 1962.
facts.tip: Apr 26 10:08 PM. After Pokemon Center. Last Tokyo dinner.
facts.wow: True A5 wagyu has 35%+ intramuscular fat (vs ~6% for top USDA Prime). That marbling is why it melts at body temperature.
facts.local: Most '5-generation' meat shops are post-WW2 lineage. Japan's old wagyu trade was disrupted, then rebuilt from the 1950s onward.

facts.kid: A traditional fried-pork-cutlet lunch with shredded cabbage. Your first meal with the team.
facts.tip: Apr 20 12:54 PM. 4 people: Bryan + 3 colleagues.
facts.wow: Tonkatsu was invented in 1899 in Tokyo as a Western adaptation. 'Katsu' comes from the English word 'cutlet.'
facts.local: The shredded raw cabbage isn't garnish - it's served first, intentionally, to help digest the heavy pork. Pile it on; eat it first.

facts.kid: Japan's most famous yellow-and-black drugstore chain. Tourists come for skincare and snacks.
facts.wow: Matsumoto Kiyoshi has 1,700+ stores. The yellow signs are designed to be visible from 200m away.
facts.local: For real deals, hit a SUNDRUG or COSMOS - same products often 10-20% cheaper. Matsukiyo is the tourist default.

facts.kid: Don Quijote — chaotic Japanese discount store with EVERYTHING.
facts.tip: Apr 19 evening — VT CICA Korean masks confirmed in haul
facts.wow: Each Donki stocks ~50,000 items, intentionally chaotic to feel like a treasure hunt. The maze layout is BY DESIGN.
facts.local: The Don Pen penguin mascot has its own Twitter account in 5 languages and posts memes daily.

facts.kid: 🎮 A WHOLE STORE of nothing but Pokemon stuff — cards, plushies, T-shirts, even snacks!
facts.tip: Apr 26 8:38-8:45 PM. 22 items, ¥35,213 total. Charizard coin purse + cards in the haul.
facts.wow: The Pokemon Company is a JOINT venture between Nintendo, Game Freak, and Creatures Inc. - not Nintendo alone, which surprises most fans.
facts.local: Each Pokemon Center sells city-exclusive Pikachu plushies in local outfits - Tokyo Tower outfit, Kyoto kimono, etc. Collector bait.

facts.kid: A modern café with free WiFi where Bryan worked on his MacBook before the CAO meeting.
facts.tip: Apr 22 9:22 AM. Cushioned seating, plants.
facts.wow: Tokyo has 600+ dedicated coworking spaces - more than NYC - but most locals just work at chain cafes (Doutor, Komeda).
facts.local: Cafe-as-office etiquette: order something every 90 min, or get politely asked to leave.

facts.kid: A modern Tokyo café with healthy grain bowls. Pink radish + tuna + herbs + coffee.
facts.tip: Apr 20 7:17 AM. Pre-team-meeting breakfast.
facts.wow: Hawaiian acai bowls hit Tokyo around 2014; now Shibuya/Daikanyama alone has dozens of variations.
facts.local: A real Japanese breakfast is rice + miso + grilled fish + tsukemono. Bowl breakfasts are 100% imported and Instagram-driven.

facts.kid: A futuristic metal-and-glass mega-station that looks like a spaceship — surprising in old Kyoto!
facts.tip: Arrived from Tokyo Sat AM, departed back on NOZOMI 28 (15:01 Sun)
facts.wow: Hiroshi Hara's 1997 design hides a 15-story 'Sky Garden' on the roof - a free public observation deck most tourists miss.
facts.local: From the rooftop terrace you can see Higashi-Honganji, the Toji pagoda, AND the mountains Bryan hiked. Best free view in Kyoto.

facts.kid: 10,000 bright orange torii gates climbing a mountain! Each donated by a family or business. You hiked deep into Mt. Inari with companions.
facts.history: Founded 711 AD. Head shrine of 30,000 Inari shrines across Japan.
facts.deity: Inari Ōkami — Shinto god/goddess of rice, foxes, and prosperity
facts.ritual: Foxes (kitsune) are Inari's messengers — fox statues hold keys or scrolls.
facts.symbol: Endless tunnel of vermilion torii gates.
facts.wow: The '10,000 torii' is folk talk - real count is closer to 32,000 including miniatures, each paid for by an individual or business praying for prosperity.
facts.local: Skip the famous Senbon Torii crowd-tunnel. The back trails above the Yotsutsuji intersection are nearly empty even at midday - exactly where Bryan went.

facts.kid: A small but historic Shinto shrine called 'Kyoto's Ise' because it's modeled after the famous Ise Grand Shrine. It has a sacred cave and a small spring.
facts.history: Founded ~5th century AD according to legend — one of the OLDEST shrines in Kyoto.
facts.deity: Amaterasu Ōmikami — Shinto sun goddess (and ancestor of the Imperial line)
facts.ritual: Pass through the cave shrine of Amano-Iwato to symbolically rebirth
facts.symbol: Inner shrine modeled after Ise + a sacred spring
facts.wow: 'Daijingu' means 'great divine shrine' - only Ise-affiliated shrines may use the title. Himukai got it because legend says Amaterasu rested here.
facts.local: The Amano-Iwato cave shrine reenacts the myth of the sun goddess hiding in a cave. Crawling through it = symbolic rebirth.

facts.kid: An 80+ KM official hiking trail that loops the mountains around Kyoto. You hiked the Higashiyama section — marker #37 photo proves it!
facts.tip: Apr 26 11:43 AM trail marker. Led to Himukai Daijingu.
facts.wow: The Higashiyama section links 9 World Heritage temples - including Kiyomizu, Ginkaku-ji, and Nanzen-ji.
facts.local: Marker #37 sits north of Nanzen-ji, near the Philosopher's Path. Most Kyoto tourists never know the trail exists.

facts.kid: Old neighborhood where you might still see GEISHA walking to work! Wooden machiya houses, lanterns, stone streets.
facts.tip: Dusk walk Sat night + Sun morning with etiquette signs
facts.wow: Real geiko (Kyoto's word for geisha) number around 80 active. Tourist photo-harassment got so bad some Gion private streets banned non-resident photography in 2024.
facts.local: The geiko you might glimpse at dusk are heading TO work, not posing. Don't follow, don't photograph, don't touch.

facts.kid: Kyoto's main river with stone embankments. At night, traditional restaurants light up along the banks.
facts.tip: Apr 25 7:32 PM walk along the river — your first Kyoto evening
facts.wow: In summer, restaurants extend wooden 'kawayuka' platforms over the river - Kyoto's only legal way to dine literally above moving water.
facts.local: Couples on the riverbank sit at almost exactly equal spacing (~1.8m apart) - a Kyoto urban legend that turned out to be measurably true.

facts.kid: A Japanese coffee chain (Komeda's) with a Pokemon-themed promotion! You had the Kuro-neige baumkuchen dessert.
facts.tip: Apr 25 5:41 PM, Kyoto.
facts.wow: Komeda's Coffee was founded in Nagoya in 1968 and is now Japan's #1 indie chain (vs. Starbucks #1 foreign chain).
facts.local: Their signature: free 'morning service' - order coffee 7-11 AM and get free toast + boiled egg.

facts.kid: Kyoto chocolate shop in a European-style building with a big clock.
facts.wow: Japanese craft chocolate has won 100+ International Chocolate Awards in the last decade - punching well above its size.
facts.local: Bean-to-bar shops cluster around Pontocho/Kiyamachi. Walking the river bank you'll pass 3 in 4 blocks.

facts.kid: A traditional-style hotel that gave Bryan a yukata (cotton kimono robe) to wear in the room.
facts.tip: Sat night Apr 25. Hotel breakfast Apr 26 morning.
facts.wow: Yukata supplied by Kyoto hotels are meant for in-room only, not the street - though tourist hotels increasingly accept it both ways.
facts.local: The 'no tattoos in public bath' rule is loosening at hotels that want foreign business, but stays rigid at traditional sento/onsen.

facts.kid: Temple covered in REAL GOLD!
facts.history: 1397 shogun retirement. Burned by monk 1950, rebuilt 1955.
facts.wow: Burned to the ground in 1950 by a young monk-arsonist. The current building is a 1955 replica; the gold leaf was upgraded in 1987 to 0.5 microns - 5x the original thickness.
facts.local: Skip the main path crowds. The back garden, toward the teahouse, has the BEST gold-leaf reflection in the pond.

facts.kid: Forest of GIANT bamboo — taller than a 4-story building.
facts.wow: The Iwatayama Monkey Park on the same mountain has 120+ wild Japanese macaques. You feed them through a cage - humans inside, monkeys outside.
facts.local: The bamboo grove is jammed 10 AM-3 PM. Locals go at 7 AM or after 4 PM - when it actually feels mystical.

facts.kid: Bright orange shrine at the Gion entrance. Hundreds of stone lanterns light up at night.
facts.wow: Hosts the Gion Matsuri every July - one of Japan's 3 biggest festivals, a whole month long.
facts.local: At New Year ~1 million people visit in 3 days for hatsumode (first shrine visit). By far Kyoto's most crowded moment of the year.

facts.kid: A temple on a HUGE wooden stage. Famous for its 3-stream Otowa Waterfall.
facts.tip: Earlier guess was wrong — the trail marker #37 is far north of Kiyomizu. Likely NOT visited.
facts.wow: 'Kiyomizu' means 'pure water' - the 3 Otowa waterfall streams each grant a different wish: longevity, success, or love. You can drink only one.
facts.local: The Edo-era idiom 'jumping off Kiyomizu's stage' (a leap of faith) comes from 234 recorded jumps off the 13m platform - 85% survived.
